intelligence.human_view: A car's dashboard puts the speed in big numerals in front of your face, and the little dials for oil and temperature off to the sides. Nobody would accept a car where the oil gauge was huge and the speed was tiny print. Same panel, same law: the number you steer by is the biggest thing you see.
intelligence.simple_view: On a scoreboard at a football game, the score is HUGE — you can read it from the far end of the field. The little clock and the team logos are smaller. That's because the score is the most important thing. Pages work the same way: biggest thing = most important thing.
intelligence.grandma_view: My bank statement used to put the balance in the same small print as everything else, and I needed a magnifier and a quiet room. The new one puts the balance big at the top. Nothing about my money changed — but I finally know where I stand in five seconds. That's all this law is asking for.
intelligence.naya_view: Assert hero order in review: number first, gauge second, ornament last. Reuse the canonical gauge; flag any new dial as a defect. Verify proportions from rendered screenshots at phone and desktop widths, never from CSS values alone.
